action.description:
When the action is CUSTOM, customProvider must be specified.
When the action is ALLOW, only requests matching the policy will be allowed.
When the action is DENY, only requests matching the policy will be denied.

When a request arrives, the policies are evaluated in the following order:
1. If there is a CUSTOM policy that matches the request, the CUSTOM policy is evaluated using the custom authorization providers and the request is denied if the provider rejects the request.
2. If there are any DENY policies that match the request, the request is denied.
3. If there are no ALLOW policies for the resource or if any of the ALLOW policies match the request, the request is allowed.
4. Else the request is denied by default if none of the configured AuthzPolicies with ALLOW action match the request. Possible values: ["ALLOW", "DENY", "CUSTOM"]
action.rationale: ALLOW, DENY and CUSTOM are all valid authorization strategies. The secure choice depends on the purpose of the policy and the surrounding rule set, so no single action can be enforced generically.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This setting controls whether the authorization policy can be destroyed or removed from Terraform management. A policy should require PREVENT so an active access-control policy cannot be deleted or abandoned unintentionally.

description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: This field is human-readable metadata only and does not change authorization matching or enforcement.

labels.description:
Set of labels associated with the AuthzExtension resource.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are resource metadata used for organisation and management. Their values do not directly change authorization behaviour, so no generic security value can be enforced.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: Identifier. Name of the AuthzPolicy resource.
name.rationale: This field identifies the AuthzPolicy resource. The correct name is deployment-specific and does not itself determine authorization behaviour.

policy_profile.description:
Defines the type of authorization being performed. 'REQUEST_AUTHZ' applies to request authorization. CUSTOM
authorization policies with Authz extensions will be allowed with ext_authz or ext_proc protocols. Extensions are
invoked only once when the request headers arrive. 'CONTENT_AUTHZ' applies to content security, sanitization, etc.
Only CUSTOM action is allowed in this policy profile. AuthzExtensions in the custom provider must support ext_proc
protocol and be capable of receiving all ext_proc events (REQUEST_HEADERS, REQUEST_BODY, REQUEST_TRAILERS,
RESPONSE_HEADERS, RESPONSE_BODY, RESPONSE_TRAILERS) with FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED body send mode. Possible values: ["REQUEST_AUTHZ", "CONTENT_AUTHZ"]
policy_profile.rationale: REQUEST_AUTHZ and CONTENT_AUTHZ serve different legitimate authorization use cases. The appropriate profile depends on the policy design and provider capabilities, so neither value is universally required.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This field selects the project that owns the resource. The correct project is environment-specific and cannot be constrained by a generic security policy.

custom_provider.description: Required if the action is CUSTOM. Allows delegating authorization decisions to Cloud IAP or to Service Extensions. One of cloudIap or authzExtension must be specified.

custom_provider.authz_extension.description: Delegate authorization decision to user authored Service Extension. Only one of cloudIap or authzExtension can be specified.

custom_provider.authz_extension.resource.description: A list of references to authorization extensions that will be invoked for requests matching this policy. Limited to 1 custom provider.
custom_provider.authz_extension.resource.rationale: This field references the authorization extension used by a CUSTOM policy. The correct extension is deployment-specific, and the provider already limits the number of referenced custom providers.

custom_provider.cloud_iap.description: Delegates authorization decisions to Cloud IAP. Applicable only for managed load balancers. Enabling Cloud IAP at the AuthzPolicy level is not compatible with Cloud IAP settings in the BackendService. Enabling IAP in both places will result in request failure. Ensure that IAP is enabled in either the AuthzPolicy or the BackendService but not in both places.

custom_provider.cloud_iap.enabled.description: Enable Cloud IAP at the AuthzPolicy level.
custom_provider.cloud_iap.enabled.rationale: Whether Cloud IAP is enabled at the AuthzPolicy level depends on the deployment architecture. The documentation notes that enabling IAP here conflicts with enabling it on the BackendService, so requiring either true or false generically could break a valid configuration.

http_rules.description:
A list of authorization HTTP rules to match against the incoming request.A policy match occurs when at least one HTTP rule matches the request or when no HTTP rules are specified in the policy. At least one HTTP Rule is required for Allow or Deny Action.
Limited to 5 rules.

http_rules.when.description: CEL expression that describes the conditions to be satisfied for the action. The result of the CEL expression is ANDed with the from and to. Refer to the CEL language reference for a list of available attributes.
http_rules.when.rationale: This CEL expression defines application-specific conditions for an HTTP authorization rule. Its secure contents depend on the intended access-control logic, so there is no universal expression or value to enforce.

http_rules.from.description: Describes properties of one or more sources of a request.

http_rules.from.not_sources.description: Describes the negated properties of request sources. Matches requests from sources that do not match the criteria specified in this field. At least one of sources or notSources must be specified. Limited to 1 not_source.

http_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.description: A list of IP addresses or IP address ranges to match against the source IP address of the request. Limited to 10 ipBlocks per Authorization Policy

http_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.le.description: The length of the address range.
http_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.le.rationale: This field defines the prefix length of an authorization negated source range. Appropriate network ranges depend on the environment, and the effect of a broader or narrower range also depends on whether the surrounding rule allows, denies, or negates the match, so no single value is universally secure.

http_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.pr.rationale: This field defines the address prefix of an authorization negated source range. Valid source networks are environment-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic prefix can be enforced.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.description:
A list of identities derived from the client's certificate. This field will not match on a request unless mutual TLS is enabled for the Forwarding rule or Gateway. Each identity is a string whose value is matched against the URI SAN, or DNS SAN or the subject field in the client's certificate. The match can be exact, prefix, suffix or a substring match. One of exact, prefix, suffix or contains must be specified.
Limited to 5 principals.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.c.description:
The input string must have the substring specified here. Note: empty contains match is not allowed, please use regex instead.
Examples:
* abc matches the value xyz.abc.def
http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.c.rationale: This field defines a contains match against a certificate-derived principal. The correct identity pattern is organisation-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic value can be enforced.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.e.description:
The input string must match exactly the string specified here.
Examples:
* abc only matches the value abc.
http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.e.rationale: This field defines a exact match against a certificate-derived principal. The correct identity pattern is organisation-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic value can be enforced.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.i.description: If true, indicates the exact/prefix/suffix/contains matching should be case insensitive. For example, the matcher data will match both input string Data and data if set to true.
http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.i.rationale: This setting controls case sensitivity for a certificate-principal matcher. Whether case-insensitive matching is appropriate depends on the identity format and on whether the surrounding rule allows, denies, or negates the match, so neither boolean value is universally secure.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.p.description:

Examples:
* abc matches the value abc.xyz
http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.p.rationale: This field defines a prefix match against a certificate-derived principal. The correct identity pattern is organisation-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic value can be enforced.

http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.p.description: An enum to decide what principal value the principal rule will match against. If not specified, the PrincipalSelector is CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN. Default value: "CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN" Possible values: ["PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED", "CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN", "CLIENT_CERT_DNS_NAME_SAN", "CLIENT_CERT_COMMON_NAME"]
http_rules.from.not_sources.principals.p.rationale: The enum accepts PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED alongside explicit client certificate identity selectors. A policy can forbid PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED so an explicit URI SAN, DNS SAN, or common-name selector must be chosen without mandating which valid selector is used.

http_rules.from.sources.description: Describes the properties of a request's sources. At least one of sources or notSources must be specified. Limited to 1 source. http_rules.to.description: Describes properties of one or more targets of a request

http_rules.to.not_operations.description: Describes the negated properties of the targets of a request. Matches requests for operations that do not match the criteria specified in this field. At least one of operations or notOperations must be specified. Limited to 1 not_operation.

http_rules.to.not_operations.methods.description: A list of HTTP methods to match against. Each entry must be a valid HTTP method name (GET, PUT, POST, HEAD, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS). It only allows exact match and is always case sensitive.
http_rules.to.not_operations.methods.rationale: This field selects HTTP methods for a negated operation match. Which methods should be authorized or denied is application-specific, so no universal method list can be enforced.

http_rules.to.not_operations.header_set.description: A list of headers to match against in http header.

http_rules.to.not_operations.header_set..description: A list of headers to match against in http header. The match can be one of exact, prefix, suffix, or contains (substring match). The match follows AND semantics which means all the headers must match. Matches are always case sensitive unless the ignoreCase is set. Limited to 10 matches.
Specifies the name of the header in the request.
http_rules.to.not_operations.header_set..rationale: This field identifies the request header used by a negated authorization operation match. The relevant header name is application-specific, so no generic value can be required.

http_rules.to.not_operations.header_set..description: Specifies how the header match will be performed.

The input string must have the substring specified here. Note: empty contains match is not allowed, please use regex instead.
Examples:
* abc matches the value xyz.abc.def
http_rules.to.not_operations.header_set..rationale: This field defines a contains match for a negated HTTP header value. The expected value is application-specific and the security effect depends on the surrounding authorization action, so no generic matcher value can be enforced.

http_rules.to.operations.mcp.description: Defines the MCP protocol attributes to match on. MCP based match is allowed only when the AuthzPolicy points to an AgentGateway.

http_rules.to.operations.mcp.base_protoc.description: If specified, matches on the MCP protocol’s non-access specific methods namely: * initialize/ * completion/ * logging/ * notifications/ * ping Default value: "SKIP_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS" Possible values: ["SKIP_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS", "MATCH_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS"]

http_rules.to.operations.mcp.methods.description: Defines a set of MCP methods and associated parameters to match on. It is recommended to use this field to match on tools, prompts and resource accesses while setting the includeBaseProtocolMethods to true to match on all the other MCP protocol methods.

http_rules.to.operations.mcp.methods.nam.description:

1) “tools”, “prompts”, “resources” - these will match against all sub methods under the respective methods.
2) “prompts/list”, “tools/list”, “resources/list”, “resources/templates/list”
3) “prompts/get”, “tools/call”, “resources/subscribe”, “resources/unsubscribe”, “resources/read”
Params cannot be specified for categories 1) and 2).
http_rules.to.operations.mcp.methods.nam.rationale: This field selects the MCP method or method category to match. The methods that should be authorized or denied depend on the Agent Gateway's capabilities and policy intent, so no generic method can be required.

network_rules.description:
A list of authorization HTTP rules to match against the incoming request.A policy match occurs when at least one HTTP rule matches the request or when no HTTP rules are specified in the policy. At least one HTTP Rule is required for Allow or Deny Action.
Limited to 5 rules.

network_rules.from.description: Describes properties of one or more sources of a request.

network_rules.from.not_sources.description: Describes the negated properties of request sources. Matches requests from sources that do not match the criteria specified in this field. At least one of sources or notSources must be specified. Limited to 1 not_source.

network_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.description: A list of IP addresses or IP address ranges to match against the source IP address of the request. Limited to 10 ipBlocks per Authorization Policy
The length of the address range.
network_rules.from.not_sources.ip_blocks.rationale: This field defines the prefix length of an authorization negated source range. Appropriate network ranges depend on the environment, and the effect of a broader or narrower range also depends on whether the surrounding rule allows, denies, or negates the match, so no single value is universally secure.

This field defines the address prefix of an authorization negated source range. Valid source networks are environment-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic prefix can be enforced.

network_rules.from.not_sources.principal.description:
A list of identities derived from the client's certificate. This field will not match on a request unless mutual TLS is enabled for the Forwarding rule or Gateway. Each identity is a string whose value is matched against the URI SAN, or DNS SAN or the subject field in the client's certificate. The match can be exact, prefix, suffix or a substring match. One of exact, prefix, suffix or contains must be specified.
Limited to 5 principals.

An enum to decide what principal value the principal rule will match against. If not specified, the PrincipalSelector is CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN. Default value: "CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN" Possible values: ["PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED", "CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN", "CLIENT_CERT_DNS_NAME_SAN", "CLIENT_CERT_COMMON_NAME"]
network_rules.from.not_sources.principal.rationale: The enum accepts PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED alongside explicit client certificate identity selectors. A policy can forbid PRINCIPAL_SELECTOR_UNSPECIFIED so an explicit URI SAN, DNS SAN, or common-name selector must be chosen without mandating which valid selector is used.

network_rules.from.not_sources.principal.description:
Required. A non-empty string whose value is matched against the principal value based on the principalSelector.
Only exact match can be applied for CLIENT_CERT_URI_SAN, CLIENT_CERT_DNS_NAME_SAN, CLIENT_CERT_COMMON_NAME selectors.

The input string must match exactly the string specified here.
Examples:
* abc only matches the value abc.
network_rules.from.not_sources.principal.rationale: This field defines a exact match against a certificate-derived principal. The correct identity pattern is organisation-specific, and the security effect depends on the surrounding allow, deny, or negated rule, so no generic value can be enforced.

Within a single source, the match follows AND semantics across fields and OR semantics within a single field, i.e. a match occurs when ANY principal matches AND ANY ipBlocks match.

target.description: Specifies the set of resources to which this policy should be applied to.

target.load_balancing_scheme.description:
Required when targeting forwarding rules and secure web proxy. Must not be specified when targeting Agent
Gateway. All resources referenced by this policy and extensions must share the same load balancing scheme.
For more information, refer to [Backend services overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/backend-service). Possible values: ["INTERNAL_MANAGED", "EXTERNAL_MANAGED", "INTERNAL_SELF_MANAGED"]
target.load_balancing_scheme.rationale: This field selects the load-balancing architecture used by the targeted resources. INTERNAL_MANAGED, EXTERNAL_MANAGED and INTERNAL_SELF_MANAGED are legitimate in different deployments, so no single scheme is universally secure.

target.resources.description:
A list of references to the Forwarding Rules or Secure Web Proxy Gateways or Agent Gateways on which this
policy will be applied.
target.resources.rationale: This field references the forwarding rules, Secure Web Proxy gateways, or Agent Gateways to which the policy applies. The correct targets are deployment-specific resource references, so no generic list can be enforced.
